name: Gepard SPAAG

placement_rationale.text: Gepard's own sourced engagement envelope (2-15 km) is a short-range counter-drone bracket, not an area-defense one, so 6 km sits inside its real employment range rather than at an arbitrary point. This is also where Shahed/Lancet-class threats are actually intercepted on this front — doctrine.md's sourced FPV strike range (0-10 km) and the ~30 km drone-dense corridor both describe the same near-line airspace a gun-based C-UAS system exists to cover. Kept close to the line by design: a 35mm proximity-fused round has no standoff reach to compensate for sitting further back.

cost.display: ~$2M per refurbished unit in bulk batches (a 2013-era contract priced one at ~€350K; 35mm ammunition runs roughly €560/round)

key_facts.label: Role
key_facts.value: Cold War-era system repurposed as a leading drone/cruise-missile killer

short_role: A 1970s-vintage twin-35mm anti-aircraft gun repurposed as one of the most effective, cost-per-kill counter-drone systems fielded in this war.
characteristics: Twin radar-directed 35mm autocannons, originally designed against Cold War-era jets and helicopters
Proximity-fused/programmable ammunition detonates near a small drone rather than requiring a direct hit
No longer in production — fielded units are refurbished from retired NATO stockpiles, which caps how many can be supplied
35mm ammunition resupply has itself become a strategic bottleneck, prompting new production contracts
employment_notes: Protects maneuver units and rear infrastructure against exactly the threat category — cheap loitering munitions and small attack drones — that a multi-million-dollar interceptor missile is uneconomical against. Its gun-based kill mechanism is far cheaper per engagement than a guided missile, which is precisely why a nominally obsolete system has become a valued asset.
contrast_vs_traditional: Designed for a threat (fast jets and attack helicopters) that barely appears in this war, Gepard turned out to be well suited to a threat nobody designed it for: cheap mass drone raids. With 60–70% of equipment losses on this battlefield now attributed to drones rather than artillery or direct fire, a cost-effective gun-based counter-drone system matters more than the raw sophistication of any single interceptor — a direct inversion of what counted as a 'modern' air-defense asset a decade ago.

notable_events.title: 10+ drones and 2 cruise missiles in a single engagement
notable_events.description: A Ukrainian Gepard crew reported downing more than 10 drones plus two cruise missiles in one engagement — widely cited as the clearest single demonstration of the type's cost-per-kill advantage over missile-based air defense against a mass drone raid.
